_title: Raw JSON-RPC wire exchange:  initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call
_capture: Captured verbatim from the agent's stdio transport while running the demo query against server two (claims-system). Each 'raw' object below is byte-for-byte the JSON that crossed the wire; the untouched source is wire/demo_claims__claims-system.jsonl.
_transport: MCP stdio transport: JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout
_where_the_model_call_happens: The model call happens ONLY in the host (agent.py issues chat.completions.create against Groq with the discovered tool schemas) and does NOT happen anywhere in this wire: initialize, tools/list and tools/call are plain JSON-RPC between host and server, and the server's tools/call handler executes the lookup with no LLM in the path.

_annotation: 'jsonrpc' — protocol-version marker; '2.0' means MCP rides JSON-RPC 2.0.
'id' — the host's request id (1): the server mirrors it so replies correlate to requests.
'method' — 'initialize' opens the MCP session: first message a client MUST send.
'params' — session-opening payload.
'protocolVersion' — the MCP protocol version the host offers ('2025-03-26').
'capabilities' — host capabilities (empty: the host exposes none of the optional client features).
'clientInfo' — who is connecting; here the week-9 agent host. The server may show this in its logs.
'jsonrpc' — again '2.0'.
'id' — mirrored 1, pairing this reply to frame 1's initialize request.
'result' — the success payload of initialize.
'protocolVersion' — the server agrees on the same MCP protocol version.
'capabilities' — server capabilities.
'tools' — the server advertises tool discovery; 'listChanged': false means it will not push tool-list-change notifications.
'logging' — the server supports the logging capability.
'serverInfo' — the server identifies itself; this is the third-party claims vendor's artifact (name 'claims-system', version 3.2.1).
'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'method' — 'notifications/initialized': a one-way notification telling the server the host has finished initializing.
'params' — {} (empty); both present and correct.
No 'id' is present: the JSON-RPC rule every notification obeys — notifications are fire-and-forget and MUST NOT get a reply.
'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'id' — 2, the next id after initialize (1).
'method' — 'tools/list': the TOOL DISCOVERY call — this is how the agent learns the server's tools instead of hard-coding them.
'params' — 'cursor': null means 'start from the first page' (listChanged is false, so one page is expected).

tools.name: claim_status
tools.description: Look up the current status of an insurance claim by claim number (CLM-YYYY-nnnnn): claimant, linked policy, status, reported date and claimed amount. Read-only.

tools.name: claim_adjuster_notes
tools.description: Read the adjuster's note history for one insurance claim by claim number (CLM-YYYY-nnnnn). Sensitive: notes may name claimants and their address/damage details. Read-only.

_annotation: 'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'id' — mirrored 2, pairing to frame 4's tools/list request.
'result' — the discovered tool catalog.
'tools' — a LIST of every tool this server makes available; the agent turns each into a function schema for the model.
tool 1 'claim_status' — the third-party server's claim-status lookup.
'description' — the tool description (docstring) that becomes the model's function description.
'inputSchema' — JSON Schema for the arguments the tool accepts.
tool 2 'claim_adjuster_notes' — the adjuster-note history lookup (the sensitive one; see risk_note.md).
Count from THIS reply: 2 tools exposed by the claims server (the count report adds them to the policy server's 2).
'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'method' — 'tools/call': the host executes a discovered tool by name.
'params' — the invocation.
'name' — 'claim_status', one of the names tools/list returned (never hard-coded in the agent).
'arguments' — the model-produced arguments, passed straight through from its function call.
'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'id' — mirrored 3, pairing to frame 6's tools/call request.
'result' — the tool's return value.
'content' — array of content blocks; one 'text' block whose 'text' is the JSON the lookup produced (claim CLM-2024-88120 is in_review, $25,000 claimed).
'isError' — false: this was a successful lookup, not an error. (Recoverable failures return isError=true — see error_before_after.md.)
'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'method' — 'tools/call' (second call of the same query).
'params' — 'name' 'claim_adjuster_notes': the second discovered tool, called because the query asked for the adjuster's note history too.
'arguments' — the same claim number the model was asked about.
No model runs here either — the host just forwards the model's chosen call.

Water damage to flooring and drywall, mostly the ground floor.", "2024-11-08: Estimate received. Total repair $25,000, all water-related.", "2024-11-10: Flagged for policy limit check - is this covered under Endorsement W cap?"]}

_annotation: 'jsonrpc' — '2.0'.
'id' — mirrored 4, pairing to frame 8.
'result' — the tool's return value.
'content' — the adjuster note history as one text block.
'isError' — false.
This reply leaves the server's trust boundary carrying claimant-level detail the adjuster wrote — one reason risk_note.md questions the token that reads it.
